I love Saint Nicholas.  

Saint Nicholas, good holy man,  
put on your finest robe  
and ride with it to Spain,  
bring apples from Oranges,  
plums from Damascus,  
give the little children something.

comes every year again,  
with his little horses before his wagon,

3.

diligently searching for knowledge,  
you were trained in it in a short time.  

4.

the flesh pricked with a rough cloth suppressed;  
your soul, a temple of the Holy Spirit,  
was attached to God day and night.  

5.

you zealously further cultivated virtue,  
your body waged a hard war,  
so that it would be more subject to the spirit.  

6.

your clothes were plain, yet neat,

7.  
When both your parents were dead,  
you received from their heritage a very great treasure,  
which you did not waste uselessly  
or lock away in an iron chest.  

8.  
You generously gave it to the poor,  
for you did not consider yourself the owner,  
but as a steward appointed by the Lord,  
which is why this deed of yours is also recounted:  

9.  
In Patara was a poor nobleman,  
who had three beautiful daughters by his wife;  
but when they had grown old,  
he could no longer provide for their maintenance.  

10.  
So he gave them advice,  
which was deadly bad for their souls,  
that for a piece of money they would stain their purity  
with dishonor.  

11.  
As soon as Saint Nicholas understood this,  
he went at night to the same house,  
threw in through the window a knotted cloth with gold,  
by which one daughter was saved.  

12.  
Once again he returned home,  
and threw gold once more through the window;  
whereby the second daughter got married,  
so great was the power of this hidden gold.  

13.  
He thought of the third daughter too,  
and one night brought the money into the house,  
by which he preserved her body in distress  
and her soul from death.  

14.  
O wise and merciful prelate,  
you know our slippery state,  
through which our unthinking young youth  
is soon carried away from its innocent virtue.  

15.  
Grant us from God a devout mind,  
that always purely does His will;  
give us the gold of love in our shoe,  
so that we avoid the punishment of God's rod.  

For him, whether of money or treats,  
has spent the night before Christmas:  
there you find some sugar in it,  
some money, some fruit, some more or less,  
according to what it has previously  
lived according to father’s and mother’s will:  
for if it has been too harshly shorn by the beast  
and behaved too badly,

['A white rose has grown for me, I will not pluck it: I loved Vojtíšek, I will love no more. I loved him faithfully, I carried him in my heart; I did not expect that love would deceive me. My beloved was walking down the street, wearing a hat tilted to the side; people told him: There you see your maiden. "Do not speak to me, people, about her, I cannot look at her; as soon as I see her with one eye, I immediately lower my head." If you could not look at me, why did you come to me? I did not ask you to love me. You had the door open to a sincere heart: but now it is closed, you will not enter it anymore! What did I do to you that you now hate me? I am the same as I was, so why are you ashamed of me? Is this now what I get for the sincerity I had for you; for you, dearest, I would have bled! Remember, dearest! your promises: that the Lord God would punish you, that He would not bless you. Remember, dearest! my young years: years I lost with you – there is a sentence after joy! I would have taken a livelihood, yet I did not give it to myself: eternity greater than the whole world, that is what I feared.', 'When I walked through the oak forest, drowsiness overcame me; and by morning, rosemary had blossomed behind my head. I cut all the green rosemary twigs, set them afloat on the water, on the cold water. The maiden who will catch the green rosemary will be my dearest by the cold water. The maidens went to the river in the morning, filling buckets: then those rosemary twigs were floating right to the footbridge. Anička, the miller’s daughter, leaned over the twigs and, unfortunate little dove, fell into the water. 

1) Bells ring, bells ring three times, what could that mean? Tell me, you little birds! Surely it’s not my beloved? "Your beloved, your joy, they are laying in a coffin; four men in black robes are putting her in the grave." 

Ah, my dearest God! You have taken my bride from me! Tell me, you little birds, the way to her grave. "Behind the hill, in the little church, priests are singing in the choir; five steps behind the little church, in the grave, lies your beloved." 

There I will go, I will weep, I will sit on that dark grave, and for you, my maiden, I will bear a heavy sorrow. I will bear the heavy sorrow until death frees me, and a wreath of rosemary will be laid on my shroud!', 'Water flows, it flows down the creek to the river: a young soldier spoke to a blue-eyed girl. Oh mother, dear mother! give me advice: a young soldier has started to follow me. "Oh daughter, my daughter! leave the soldier alone: soldiers will ride away, you will be left alone." Oh mother, dear mother! your advice is bad: I have already tied my dress, I will go with the soldiers. Soldiers, soldiers! you have beautiful horses: I would also like to ride with you, which one will you give me? "No other than the black one: he will be nicely saddled, you will sit on him." After a year, she returned to her mother, carrying a little soldier wrapped in a spotted blanket. Oh mother, dear mother! help me now: my baby will call you: Grandma! "Oh daughter, my daughter! my advice was bad: may whoever gave you that advice now help you!" Oh God, oh great God! what was I thinking that I did not want to obey my dear mother! Now I am alone, like a little dove flying into the world, searching for a mate. Now I am alone, like a pear tree in the field: when the pears are picked, it stands sad. Now I am alone, like a post by the road: only now do I realize the misfortune I have!']

["At the hour of the Rat, life is born in heaven; the Breath is active like the hour of the Serpent.  
The clear sky is 'Heaven' (천).  
At the hour of the Ox, life is born, receiving the Five Elements,  
nurturing all things that grow.  
The mysterious black color of latent illnesses corresponds to the north and the Black Tortoise (현무).  
The palace shapes and colors correspond to the four directions: east, west, south, north; the center is earth-colored yellow.  
The distance of heaven and earth spans tens of thousands of li, with fire, earth, river, and flowers forming a home.  
The rise and fall of generations occur in the firm palace houses of kings.  
Laughing at the flood, the stars of the Rat appear, holding the map of the nine districts.  
The system of longevity corresponds to the jade bell class; the king is the rough yellow son.  
The sages Yao and Shun appear majestic, with earthly branches corresponding to the year, month, and day.  
The countless creatures move and breathe, governed by the observance of the year and month, the moon being the moon’s sign.  
The star Osiris is the guardian of the stomach gate, a bright star of the palace.  
Long spring days and steady nights require constant management and effort.  
The twenty-eight lunar mansions form the map of the heavens, centered on the red stars.  
The pitiful golden bells ring in the dormitory, and paired mandarin ducks are like well-crafted gold needles.  
The absolute beauty dwells in the right palace; elegant music and full formation spread, marking the star.  
The four months of planting and month of new life correspond to the east, south, and the field of stars.  
Wealth, honor, and fame are like a dream in the fields; giving up and resting is a well-arranged sign.  
A simple life—our life will eventually come to white hair.  
At the seasonal turning of spring, plants sprout; the sign for existence and warmth is set.  
The study hall upholds virtue and goodness; ten thousand years of peaceful hands.  
The golden flute plays; the chill cannot be fought in autumn’s pursuit.  
When white hair arrives, youth has already collected the dust of the wind.  
The cold wind blows from the river; the white snow covers the mountain winter.  
Longing without forgetting, our love is precious, building strength in body and mind.  
The lotus pond mix contains shrimps and clams, blending the lotus’s essence.  
The world’s beauty is visible day-to-day but difficult to fully encompass.  
By doing much good and accumulating merit, heaven’s work and all affairs will succeed.  
We labor like this, but once we die,  
time and years pass away.  
With a bright light, I cannot mistreat my wife; she is like the sun ruling the great order and the laws of the universe.", 'Heaven has the Northern Fairy, below the earth is Niryeo.  
With nothing to do, the great queen who built the palace,  
hangs a pair of twisted vines. “Twists,” she says, “don’t hang them.”  
But there are no twisted vines at all. In the moonlight, there are pitch pine trees,  
branches stretching eastward to the East Sea,  
cut down with a jade axe,  
refining a golden axe,  
carrying bent wood to the loom,  
tying willow branches on the back.  
If she hangs a pair of twisted vines,  
there are no places at all to hang them.  
Looking around the left and right green mountains,  
there was a jade railing,  
and three twisted vine bridges,  
the front two legs set high,  
the back two legs set low,  
and the poor sheep that lie down.  
In July, when the Seven Stars meet,  
the Cowherd and Weaver Girl reunite,  
building a magpie bridge.  
The sheep sitting on it,  
the sheep clad in fine silk,  
are like the mist around Samgaksan Mountain in Seoul.  
The sheep with curled tails seem to be the three eldest sons,  
wrapped in mourning clothes.  
The chattering and fluttering magpies,  
surround the stone cutting line.  
A rainbow at the East Sea in the east,  
a rainbow at the West Sea in the west.  
The sheep striking the northern embankment  
are like the twin dragons of the earth,  
beating against the cliffs and rivers.  
The four sheep at the black forest,  
seem like three brothers called the In Ae,  
reliant on each other, loving and hating,  
with fishing rods held by Gang Taegong.  
Throwing the bait into the water,  
waiting without October.  
It split apart, the energy,  
yujeweil said, listening carefully,  
two brothers at the evening time,  
pressed by a father who loves and hates,  
is it a courtesan shedding fallen leaves in late October?  
A naturally bent pine tree,  
hangs a noose on the green mountain,  
crosses the Jido River,  
back and forth they go.  
The sound of footsteps like a rooster  
is from Chuwang Mountain,  
standing in pairs and crying out.  
The fluttering little hands clap to fly.  
Is the fishing line also a thread?  
Such and such is the rain that weaves,  
thirty stones are thirty-six,  
catching seeds in the front stream,  
carrying them to the Milky Way,  
in Milyang village chief’s word.  
With a Hongdukke from Cheongdu Mountain,  
clattering and pounding with a bang,  
is it rising in Seoul?  
The eight fairies, with good thread,  
sew clothes; how wonderful that must be!', 'The examination is confusing, but what good is sighing alone in an empty room?  
Such is the fate of the four pillars of destiny, so my mind is restless.  
Let me try singing a twisted song:  
The twisted leg is a death sentence,  
Your leg is a single leg,  
At the time of conception, there are three legs.  
The goose caught at conception walks like the male organ;  
They sit one after another.  
Generously placing a gambler’s hand with ease,  
Playing foolishly, there is no way to resist the small songs.  
Hehe, the empty sheep sits on three legs,  
Endless with silver food, the twang of the plucked bow fades,  
Is it the sound of the lone wanderer in Gyeongju?  
The cry of the dove at dawn in the clear sky,  
Crying alone as it goes.  
The crooked tree of faith hangs its neck with worn-out rope,  
Sighs when climbing up and sighs when descending.  
The three-tiered acorn cluster withers after one morning,  
Pitiful is this fate—pulling in the front water and licking in the back water,  
Spoon by spoon, it plays and unravels like the sound of children.  
Let our husband try on a real jin robe,  
I tried searching for the thread of destiny,  
Looking frantically but life, like a matchstick, inevitably departs.  
Trying to find the ear needle,  
The ears appear and then disappear.  
Picked once, picked twice, alas this is the misfortune of heaven and earth.  
It is sealed, it is sealed, the real jin robe is sealed.  
Nothing can be done, nothing can be done, my husband, nothing can be done.  
Waiting for your return in September, beneath the willow,  
The wild chrysanthemums smell sweet, but why do they bloom so late?  
Passersby each time say our gentleman has not come,  
Passersby answer that something has passed, something is lost,  
Coming down the path of the Seven Stars board.  
Hello, sir, is that true?  
Why lie?  
Losing my mind as I chase, turning at a bend,  
The twenty-eight lunar mansions march in step.  
I trusted the three generations, but the funeral time was the beginning of the curse.  
The silk skirt that was worn was the first curse,  
The straw sandals worn on black feet were also the first curse.  
In the prime of youth, unable to help but return,  
Opening the door and answering, the mandarin duck, golden bedding, and the cabinet—  
With whom are you exchanging words? My soul is gray-haired, I am dying.  
This helpless life, helpless,  
Like raw ointment, like prevention of illness.  

When the bucket drops, it falls as one,  
Listening to the cry, it mourns in a single melody.  
A feeling of one energy, one energy—this fate is one energy.  
Though youth turned to white hair, today we part and see,  
Sighs rise and anger wells up, oh, people of the clear sky,  
Hear these words:  
Having lost a head like a mountain in one day,  
Asking the soul a hundred times, it has grown restless,  
Though my body is like this, not knowing the falling flower and freezing dew, the empty sky is being emptied.  
Hello, sir, if you hear this news, please convey it to my lord:  
Why does the goose in the clear sky wander and cry along the streets?  
Thinking of this fate, goose, goose, you too came out—  
Having lost our beloved together, crossing the Han River, this is the fortune of the world.  
Namu Amitabul Gwansembosal (Amitabha Buddha, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva).']

Name: 4_love_repeat_god_sail
Representative_Docs:
["In Vienna, in Vienna, oh yes, that beautiful city,
Which contains thousands of little soldiers,
There was a sweet girl who loved faithfully,
She had a little soldier as her best friend.
He went to desert to see his bride,
Because he knew very well it was not allowed.
They imprisoned him, oh what great sorrow,
His sentence was passed, oh yes it was: death!

The girl became furious, she immediately ran,
And threw herself on the ground before the Captain.
Oh sir Captain, free my little soldier,
Then you will make my heart joyful and happy again,
Oh sir Captain, I will give you some money,
If at least you care about that,
Oh my misfortune is great,
Spare my little soldier from the bitter death.

Your little soldier must die, that is the law,
That is what I have fixed now,
But I will give you three riddles,
If you know them, you save his life,
If you guess them, then he is saved,
If you listen to my words,
Otherwise it is over for him,
If you don't solve them, he must die.

Riddle. Tell me, does there exist a king without land?
Where is there water without sand?
What is more than all the money on earth?
What is worth millions to everyone?
How does one travel around the earth in a day?
Now, dear girl, tell me at once,
You save his life, I am listening,
Just guess it, otherwise it is over.

She. A king on a map has no land,
Water in the eyes has no sand,
Being content is the greatest treasure on earth,
Health is worth everything to people,
Stand on the sun and you certainly get there,
Because it is surely there at its appointed time.
If this answer is to your liking.
Oh save him then, I beg you sir.
He. Tell me, is there great water without fish?
Tell me what is worse than death?
Tell me who is the greatest power in every case?
Who forces itself everywhere and into everything?
Where is nothing that everyone must always have?
Be careful and guess this well again,
Oh German girl, his life depends on it,
Otherwise he undergoes his deserved punishment.

She. In the rain barrel one finds no fish.
An evil woman who is worse than death,
God is the power, which does not please everyone,
The little fly forces itself everywhere.
One must have patience as long as one lives,
No one can exist without it.
My answer is now certainly right with that,
Oh sir captain! let my little soldier free.

He. Where is a mirror, girl, without glass?
What is most useful in the world?
Where is the key that fits all locks?
What can’t be grasped, even when you try hard?
What does man not lose before his death?
Guess these now, they are very great,
If you know them, he is free.
So be well and be joyful and happy.

She. The mirror of the heart has no glass,
Tolerance is the most useful,
Money certainly opens all locks,
The mist, I believe, cannot be grasped.
Hope leaves no one as long as he lives,
Now your word of honor that you give me,
Oh sir! I have now done my duty,
Let me now happily leave you.

Both. Well then, he has mercy, he is free.
Make yourself happy, joyful and glad;
We will now marry together,
And celebrate a happy wedding,
That is according to our wish and desire,
As a reward for our tender love,
Thus a clever girl saves her lover from death,
Is such love not truly great?", "How long that journey also takes;
It is now the fourth year;
How sadly fearful that time falls upon me!
I took an East Indies sailor,
A sea dog, fresh, healthy, and strong,
Greatly loved by the ship's crew,
Also by his Officers, as I notice:
A man like a child.

Thoroughly learned in ship work,
A truly experienced man:
Who neither fights, nor swears, nor drinks, nor curses,
Who can speak fiercely
When it is necessary, and otherwise not.
Oh, if I could see him again,
There would be an end to my sorrow;
How welcome he was!
Look, whether I say it or stay silent
I am very uneasy,
Because I get no word or answer...
Who knows on which coast
The ship has come to grief! Perhaps
It perished with man and mouse...
Oh Bram, shall I never see you again?
Won't you come home to your wife!

Who knows where he travels and wanders!
Whether he suffers from hunger!
And is sick and sighing, even dying.
I may have already lost him.
It is already far beyond the year
Since I last saw his spirit;
I sat with the child, and he stood there,
By bright clear day.
He looked quite well,
So handsome, so well made:
It is certain that this means something good;
He looked earnestly at the child.
There he stood, in his long trousers,
No six feet from me;
I saw very clearly the silk cloth
That I had given him as a gift:

Naturally, tied around his neck.
How immensely happy I was!
I had long hoped for this sight.
I thought, he is thinking of me.
My Bram was never a frivolous fellow,
Says everyone who knows him.
He has a valuable intellect;
Oh, he is such a good man!
I got this child when he was still
Less than eight weeks at sea.
He was well-made in body and limb,
It went well with him.
People suspected I served for Min
Regarding that:
But I had no intention of that,
I declined the Lady.

I give my child what God gave me
For the little blood.
I also promised it to my husband, and he
Left me on this.
Come to mother, sweet Jan;
Oh, if your daddy were here!
If he saw you, I know the man
Would cry with joy.
Yes, if you only knew, my dear Bram,
How day and night,
I cared for our little lamb;
How I fulfilled my duty!
He left my sight not once;
I earned my bread with the needle.
I feared gossip more
Than the pale death.

But why do I torment myself so
And worry, and sigh, and cry.
The man probably has it well;
I can, after little time,
See him again, healthy and fresh.
That would be a joy!
‘Then it’s a new fair again’:
So says my neighbor Styn.
And see, she already knows this of old;
That I can well guess:
Sailors always have good wives,
That is all we do.
They visit us so cheerfully,
They don’t look stern or angry:
Hear, it doesn’t grieve me that for myself
I chose a handsome sailor girl.

What is the noise in the street?
It is already flying towards Westdyk...
It’s as if guns are firing too!
I’ll go and look as well;
So I get the right information;
Come with me, mother, Jan.
There lies the ship; look, Jantje, there.

Name: 11_wolf_hawk_beggar_sheep
Representative_Docs: ['In some places, they play this game without a shepherd and without a dog. The grazing sheep sing: I’m tearing, tearing little grass in that green little grove; if a wolf comes to me, he will seize my neck: I am not afraid of the wolf, I will milk my little cows: come, wolf, come! Then the wolf jumps up and the sheep start to flee, dropping the grass they had torn and saying: "Here you have, wolf, your little grass!" The wolf catches whichever sheep he can, takes it away, and then goes to lie in wait again, until he catches them all. Sr. Krolm. II, 456.', 'II. The shepherdess, the little dog, the flock of sheep, and the wolf as in the previous play. The shepherdess with the little dog walks around the flock, twirling a twig in her hand and singing: Our lady used to say that I should shepherd well; but I will not shepherd, I would rather leave here: she herself eats the malt’s porridge, and gives me whey; she herself drinks from a glass, and gives me from a shoe; she herself rides in a carriage, and I must ride on a cart. Now she calls into the forest: “Wolf! Wolf!” – The wolf runs out: “What do you want? I am the wolf.” Shepherdess: “If you are the wolf, catch the prettiest little sheep.” Wolf: “I don’t want the sheep; I want a pretty little girl!” The shepherdess runs, the wolf after her, and when he catches her, they take each other’s hands and, turning around, sing: Our lady used to say that I should shepherd well; but I will not shepherd, I would rather go away with the wolf: she herself eats etc. Meanwhile, the dog constantly barks and the flock bleats, accompanying the song. Štěpnice, 1857, p. 50.', 'The Wolf Game. I. One boy is the wolf, hiding in the bushes, behind the fence, in the ditch, etc.; the second is the shepherd, and the third is the dog. The other children, boys and girls, are the sheep, sitting on a hillock and plucking grass as if grazing. The shepherd sings: "I graze, I graze the sheep on the wolf\'s meadow; the wolf is not home, he went to Bydžov for four sheep, the fifth a ram, for a white ram with golden horns." Meanwhile, the wolf sneaks up and jumps among the sheep, which scatter; whichever he catches, he takes to his place. This game repeats as many times as there are still sheep grazing. Meanwhile, the shepherd and the dog defend their sheep, so the boy playing the wolf must be stronger than they are. When all the sheep have been taken, the wolf also catches the dog and finally the shepherd himself.']

Name: 15_goslings_john_strawberries_gate
Representative_Docs:
["We feel like singing the praise,
Of the necessary things,
Of marriage, or the power of the land,
So joyful! Our cat has kittens!
If I had now a hundred thousand tongues,
And Lord Rosthuizer his mind!
How would I, through my poetry,
Teach this lovely pair of doves to tumble!
But listen, this little herb does not move me,
Or sawing branches in the bride's garden,
Or ambushing the finch with a net.
That is best done where no one sees.
The honking of the geese, and the cackling,
Of the hen, are his oracles,
And wondrous spells of Apollo,
Full of liver veins, throats of blowholes,
Latin decorates the apothecary's pots,
Just as the miller adorns the beautiful face.
But holla, hold on ... that serpent of serpents,
Also makes my wrong nuts crack;
I had to lament about true matrimony.
And how the wives, to please,
Bear the world of the husband,
So that it does not perish.
That great porter of the globe,
At our Town Hall, is just a little egg
In the number laughed at by the woman,
Who from evening till morning:
Will care for the world's durability,
And strives for the increase of the people.
Marriage is an old custom
For Adam had a wife out of necessity;
But tell me, how would that go,
If one had to do without the female sex?
Who then would, to gather people,
Ever beat the drum of marriage?
If the female sex also had to live alone,
(Like the poets separate the Amazons,
Sorted apart from the men)
Then it would be best to create the man.
Completely defenseless and without weapons.
Who then cares for the rose wreath?
An Amazon (so to speak)
Is but a bench without a blanket,
And a little candlestick without a candle.
A little field that remains fallow.", 'For the goslings. The same game as the boys’: “At the Golden Gate.” Two girls imitate a gate, standing opposite each other and holding hands raised so that there is a passage underneath. One of them calls herself the Sun, the other the Moon. From afar comes a line of girls, the “goslings,” one after another, holding each other by the hips over their skirts; the first called the “gosling boy.” Gate: Goslings, goslings, fly! Goslings: We must not. Gate: For whom? Goslings: For the lord. Gate: The lord is not home, he went to Beroun, for a white ram with golden horns. The goslings fly toward the gate, shouting: “Honk! honk! honk!” And when the last in line tries to fly through, the gate closes, and the gosling gets caught between the Sun and the Moon. Gate: Gosling, where have you been? Gosling: In the forest. Gate: What were you doing there? Gosling: Cutting wood. Gate: What for the wood? Gosling: For the garden. Gate: What for the garden? Gosling: To plant lettuce. Gate: What for the lettuce? Gosling: To have food. Gate: For that you must, gosling, be ours. Whom will you choose: the Sun or the Moon? The gosling answers and stands behind the one she chooses. Then the gate calls again: Goslings, goslings, fly! Goslings: “We must not,” and so on, as at first. When all the goslings, including the gosling boy, have joined either the Sun or the Moon, the “Suns” and “Moons” begin to fight, each side straining to pull the other over the line, in every way, just like in the boys’ game: “At the Golden Gate.” See also Krol. I, 295. – Suš. 729. – 1) Also: for precious roots, for heart aches.', 'II. Two boys first secretly agree between themselves who will be the Angel and who will be the Devil, and with a half-step they make a gate, but each only with one hand. The other boys, holding hands, form a circle in the gate, so that one pillar of the gate is inside the circle and the other pillar is outside the circle. The circle begins to turn, and the Devil and the Angel sing as follows: Under the pit, a mouse, under the pit: come, you tomcat, come with us! The keys ring, the violet scents. The gate is open, supported by a sword: whoever touches the gate shall be beheaded. Slash! Slash! Slash! At the word “slash!” the arch is lowered for the first and second time always between two boys in the circle, and immediately lifted again; but at the third time the circle stops, and the gate asks the one in front of whom the arch was lowered: “Whom do you join?” He then answers: “You,” pointing to one or the other, not knowing whether he joined the Angel or the Devil, and stands behind him. Then the circle closes again, starts to turn, and the gate sings as in the beginning: Under the pit, a mouse, etc. This goes on until even the last one in the circle has joined either one or the other side of the gate. Then the Angel and the Devil reveal themselves, and the “Heavenly ones” and the “Hellish ones” begin to fight, pulling each other across the Line as in the previous game.']
